column1: # The shared contract as 54 argument cases. tests/run.sh runs every implementation against each row.
# Columns are tab-separated: input, exit, stderr, stdout.
#   input   the single argument passed. <none> means no argument at all; "" means an empty-string argument.
#   stderr  the exact expected stderr, without its final newline. * means not checked;
#           a glob: prefix means the rest is matched as a shell glob.
#   stdout  the exact expected stdout, without its final newline. "" means empty.
# input, stderr and stdout are decoded with printf %b, so \n is a newline and \xHH is a raw byte.
# Accepted rows run with a fake ping on PATH that answers only for host .1, so stdout is <network>.1
# and the summary is "1 host up on <network>.0/24".
# Not UTF-8: each runtime decodes the byte differently before printing it, so stderr is matched by glob.
# Well-formed network, wrong suffix: exit 1, "invalid network: <arg> (only /24 is supported)"
# Accepted: exit 0, on TEST-NET-1 (192.0.2.0/24, reserved for documentation)
# No argument: exit 2, a usage line naming the script
